Then he complained of their condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people by night and by day﴾, until he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.﴾ Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged, for they are to be drowned.﴾ That is, after today.

Noah then devoted himself to [building] the ship and withdrew from his people to a mountain, where he cut wood and struck the iron with his hands, and prepared the materials for the ship from pitch and other things that only he could prepare. His people kept passing by him while he was at his work, mocking him and saying: "O Noah, have you become a carpenter after prophethood?" Allah made the wombs of the women barren, so they remained for years without any child being born to them.

He said: The People of the Torah claim that Allah commanded him to build the ship from teak wood, and to make it with a slope, and to coat it with pitch on its bottom and outside, and that its length should be eighty cubits and its width fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, and the cubit is measured to the shoulder. He made it three stories: lower, middle, and upper. He made windows in it, and Noah did as Allah the Exalted commanded him [[The same source: 48.]].

﴿Until when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾, that is, Our punishment came and the water gushed out from the face of the earth. The Arabs call the face of the earth "the oven of the earth." This is because when it was said: "When you see water flowing over the face of the earth, then board, you and whoever follows you." Among those who said this were Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), in explaining ﴿the oven boiled over﴾, said: it means the dawn rose and the light of morning appeared, and from this is the expression "the dawn lit up" (nawwara al-fajr tanwīran). Qatadah said: it is a place on the earth and the highest place in it. Al-Hasan said: by the oven he meant the one in which bread is baked. It was an oven of stone that belonged to Eve, until it came to Noah, and it was said to him: "When you see the water boiling out of the oven, board, you and your companions." Water gushed from the oven, and his wife learned of it and informed him. This is the saying of Mihran [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/33, the saying of al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ata' from Ibn Abbas.]]. It was transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

Mujahid said: this occurred in the region of Kufah. Al-Suddi narrated from al-Sha'bi that he used to swear by Allah that the oven appeared only from the region of Kufah. He said: Noah built the ship in the middle of the mosque of Kufah, and the oven was on the right of one entering from the direction of the Kindah Gate, and the gushing of the water from it was a sign for Noah and an indication of the destruction of his people.

Muqatil said: that oven was the oven of Adam, and it was in Syria, in a place called 'Ayn Wardah. Ibn Abbas said: "the oven boiled over" in India. The "fawr" is boiling.

﴿We said: "Load into it﴾, that is, into the ship, ﴿two of each pair﴾. The commentators said: by the pairs he meant two, a male and a female. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: every two that cannot do without one another; the Arabs call each of them a "zawj" (pair). It is said: "a pair of sandals" if he has two sandals; similarly, "a pair of doves," and "a pair of shackles." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female.﴾ Some said: by the pairs he meant the types and kinds, and every type is called a zawj. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that he wears / Abu Qudamah is loved for that, both together"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/55.]]

He meant every type and color. Labid said:

"And one [.....] [[Unreadable word.]] the charge of the warriors, a power / and their kinds [........] [[Unreadable word.]] drinks"

meaning colors and kinds. Hafs read here and in Surah al-Mu'minun "min kullin" with tanwin, meaning "from every kind," and took "ithnayn" (two) as emphasis.

﴿And your family﴾, that is, carry your family, your property and your dependents, ﴿except those against whom the word has already been decreed﴾ of destruction, meaning his wife, who was left behind, and his son Canaan.

﴿And those who have believed﴾, meaning carry those who have believed in you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ They differed about their number. Qatadah, al-Hakam, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: there was in the ship only Noah and his wife, and his three sons: Sam, Ham and Japheth, the brothers of Canaan, and their wives, so all of them were eight. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah invoked Allah to change his sperm, and so he produced the black people.

Al-A'mash said: they were seven: Noah, three wives, and his three sons. Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten apart from their wives: Noah, his sons Ham, Sam and Japheth, and six people from among those who had believed with him, and their wives, all together.

Muqatil said: [they were] seventy-two men and women, and his three sons and their wives, so the total was seventy-eight souls, half of them men and half of them women.

Ibn Abbas said: there were eighty people in the ship of Noah, one of them being Jurhum [[Likewise in Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/57. In Tarikh Dimashq (62/267): with them were their families.]].

Muqatil said: Noah carried with him the body of Adam and placed it crosswise between the men and the women. Noah carried all the animals, the sheep, the wild beasts and the birds, and separated them from one another.

Ibn Abbas said: the first animal Noah loaded into the ship was the goose, and the last he loaded was the donkey. When the donkey entered and its chest went in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its legs could not move forward. Noah kept saying to it: "Enter," and it would stand up but not walk, until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter even if the devil is with you." Noah said to him: "What brought you to me, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Did you not say 'Enter even if the devil is with you'?" Noah said: "Get out of my sight, O enemy of Allah." He said: "You have no choice but to carry me with you." So, as they claim, he was on the back of the ship [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/49.]].

In the Tafsir of Malik ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi, who informed me with the chain of narration to Abu al-Qasim and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad (part of it by reading, and he permitted me the rest on more than one occasion), he said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Harawi narrates to us, saying: Jabir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us from him that the snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: "Carry us." So whoever recites, when fearing their harm: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds. Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good. Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾, neither of them will harm him.

In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (9/21) there is disagreement regarding some of the opinions.]] said: they were humble before Him. It was also said [[This is Ibn Qutaybah, as in Zad al-Masir.]] that they were modest toward Him.

Will you not then remember?﴾ Al-Farra' said: He did not say "Are they equal in likeness" (in the plural), because the blind and the deaf are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the disbeliever, while the hearing and the seeing are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the believer.

The rest read it with a kasra, "innī," saying: because sending (irsal) carries the meaning of saying.

﴿Painful﴾ (alīm) means ﴿painful﴾ (mu'lim). Muqatil said: Noah was sent, and his Lord commanded him to build the ark when he was six hundred years old. His lifespan was one thousand and fifty years, and he remained calling his people for nine hundred and fifty years. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he remained among them one thousand years less fifty years﴾, that is, remaining among them as a caller.

﴿And we see for you no superiority over us; rather we think you are liars.﴾ Noah said: ﴿O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy (guidance and forgiveness) from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you? ﴿The chiefs of those who disbelieved from among his people said: "We see you as nothing but a human like ourselves, and we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us, immature in judgment."﴾ That is: human like ourselves (ādamiyyan mithlanā); ﴿the lowest of us﴾ means the basest of us; ﴿immature in judgment﴾ (bādiya al-ra'y) was read by Mujahid, Abu al-Mu'in, Hamzah, Abu 'Amr and Basir with the meaning of bādiya al-ra'y, without deliberation or reflection; that is, they believed without deliberation.

﴿And we see for you no superiority over us; rather we think you are liars.﴾ Noah said: ﴿O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy (guidance and forgiveness) from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you? Shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾ It was made obscure: it became confused and unclear. The people of Kufah read "fa-'ummiyat" with a damma on the ayn and shaddah on the mim, meaning it became unclear and was confused. The meaning of the statement is: the eyes were blinded to the truth. This is like saying: "The ring entered my finger" or "the khuff (boot) entered my foot," while in reality the finger enters the ring and the foot enters the boot. ﴿Shall we compel you to it﴾ means the evidence and mercy. ﴿While you are averse to it﴾ means you do not want it, that is, it is not accepted.

﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth in return for it﴾, that is, for the revelation and conveying the message, which is an allusion to something unmentioned. ﴿My reward is only from Allah.﴾ ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed; indeed they will meet their Lord﴾ with the Resurrection, so He will reward them for their deeds. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾ ﴿And O my people, who will support me against Allah if I drive them away? Then will you not remember?﴾ The "bā'" in ﴿and I will not drive away﴾ is extra (ṣilah).

﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon (tazdarī: despise and belittle) that Allah will never give them any good.﴾ That is: it will be taken away from them. ﴿Allah knows best what is within themselves﴾ of intention, resolve, good and evil. ﴿Indeed I, then, would be among the wrongdoers﴾ if I did that.

﴿They said: "O Noah, you have argued with us and have disputed with us at length, so bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful."﴾ ﴿He said: "Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not escape. My advice will not benefit you, even if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you (yughwiya: destroy and lead astray) — He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned."﴾ ﴿He is your Lord﴾, and the command and judgment belong to Him. This is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah [a rationalist theological school] and the Murji'ah [a theological school on faith and deeds].

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Ibn Abbas said: it refers to Noah. Muqatil said: it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime (my sin and the burden of my affair); you will not be held accountable for my sin, and I am free of what you commit."﴾ ﴿I will not be taken to account for your sins.﴾

﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "No one of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed (tabta'is: be grieved) by what they have been doing."﴾ ﴿Indeed I will destroy them and deliver you from them.﴾ Then he invoked against them and said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant (dayyāran).﴾

﴿And construct the ship﴾ and make the boat ﴿before Our eyes﴾, that is, in Our sight. Al-Dahhak said: in Our view. Muqatil said: with Our knowledge. Al-Rabi' said: in Our hearing [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: in Our protection.]].

﴿And by Our revelation﴾ [according to what We revealed to you]. Ibn Abbas said: this is because he did not know how to construct the ship, so Allah revealed to him that he should build it in the shape of the breast of a bird. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed they are to be drowned﴾ by the flood. He was commanded not to intercede for them with Him, and it was said that this referred to his wife and son.

﴿And he was constructing the ship.﴾ It was said: its meaning is "and he was constructing," and it was said: its meaning is "and he constructed." ﴿Whenever a company of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him.﴾ That is, they mocked him.

He said: ﴿If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule us now, and you will come to know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment (muqīm: enduring).﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Noah (peace be upon him) built the ship over two years. Its length was three hundred cubits, its width was fifty, and its height was thirty cubits. It was made of teak wood. He made it three levels: in the lowest level he placed the wild animals, predators and vermin; in the middle level, the beasts and livestock; and he himself boarded in the top level [.....] [[Unreadable text.]]

, of what was needed from provisions.

It is narrated from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Noah remained among his people one thousand years less fifty years, calling them to Allah. When his time was nearly over, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him, and he planted a tree [it grew greatly and spread in every direction, then he cut it] [[Addition from al-Tabari.]] and cut off what dried out from it. Then he began to build a ship, and his people would pass by him and ask him, and he would say: 'I am building a ship.' They would mock him and say: 'He is building a ship on dry land, how will it sail?' He would say: 'You will come to know.' When he finished it, and the oven boiled over and the water increased in the streets, the mother of a child became anxious for him, for she loved him very dearly. She took him to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she reached two-thirds of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she climbed to the top of the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him with her hands until the water carried them both away. So if Allah had shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."

It was narrated by Ali ibn Zayd ibn Suhan from Yusuf ibn Mihran from Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said to Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both: "If only you would send us a man who witnessed the ship, so he could tell us about it." So he took them until he reached a mound of earth. He took a handful of that earth in his palm and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the shroud of Ham son of Noah." He struck the mound with his staff and said: "Rise by the permission of Allah." Immediately he was standing, shaking the dust from his head, and he had grown gray. Jesus said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No, I died while I was young, but I thought it was the Hour, so that is why I turned gray." He said: "Tell us about the ship of Noah." He said: "Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits, and it had three levels: one level contained the beasts and wild animals, one level contained the humans, and one level contained the birds. When the dung of the animals increased, Allah the Exalted revealed to Noah: 'Rub the tail of the elephant.' He rubbed it, and a male and female pig fell from it, and they came to the dung. When the mouse fell into the ship's bilge and its ropes, it gnawed them, because the mouse had given birth in the ship. Allah the Exalted revealed to Noah: 'Strike between the eyes of the lion.' He struck it, and a cat and a tomcat came out of its nostril, and they went after the mice."

Jesus said to him: "How did Noah know that the lands had drowned?" He said: "He sent the raven to bring him news. It found a carcass and settled on it, so he invoked fear upon it. That is why it does not get used to houses. Then he sent the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and mud on its foot, so he knew that the lands had drowned." He said: "He placed a red collar around its neck and prayed for it that it would be in a palace in safety [[In Tafsir al-Tabari: 'Anas' and 'Aman'.]]." That is why it gets used to houses.

He said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take him to our families so that he may sit with us and speak to us?" He said: "How can one who has no provision follow you?" Then he said to him: "Return by the permission of Allah." He said: So he returned to dust [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/47.]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Ubayd ibn Umayr that he used to tell stories, and they (the people of Noah) would seize him and choke him until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he would say: "My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know." Until they persisted in disobedience, great sin spread upon the earth from them, and they became arrogant toward him, and the affair became arrogant toward him and against them. Hardship against him from them intensified, and miserliness followed miserliness. No generation came except that it was more wicked than the one before it, until the last of them would say: "This is what our fathers and grandfathers had, just like this," as a madman, and they would not accept anything from him. Then he complained of their condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people by night and by day﴾, until he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.﴾ Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged, for they are to be drowned.﴾ That is, after today.

Noah then devoted himself to [building] the ship and withdrew from his people to a mountain, where he cut wood and struck the iron with his hands, and prepared the materials for the ship from pitch and other things that only he could prepare. His people kept passing by him while he was at his work, mocking him and saying: "O Noah, have you become a carpenter after prophethood?" Allah made the wombs of the women barren, so they remained for years without any child being born to them.

He said: The People of the Torah claim that Allah commanded him to build the ship from teak wood, and to make it with a slope, and to coat it with pitch on its bottom and outside, and that its length should be eighty cubits and its width fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, and the cubit is measured to the shoulder. He made it three stories: lower, middle, and upper. He made windows in it, and Noah did as Allah the Exalted commanded him [[The same source: 48.]].

﴿Until when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾, that is, Our punishment came and the water gushed out from the face of the earth. The Arabs call the face of the earth "the oven of the earth." This is because when it was said: "When you see water flowing over the face of the earth, then board, you and whoever follows you." Among those who said this were Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), in explaining ﴿the oven boiled over﴾, said: it means the dawn rose and the light of morning appeared, and from this is the expression "the dawn lit up" (nawwara al-fajr tanwīran). Qatadah said: it is a place on the earth and the highest place in it. Al-Hasan said: by the oven he meant the one in which bread is baked. It was an oven of stone that belonged to Eve, until it came to Noah, and it was said to him: "When you see the water boiling out of the oven, board, you and your companions." Water gushed from the oven, and his wife learned of it and informed him. This is the saying of Mihran [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/33, the saying of al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ata' from Ibn Abbas.]]. It was transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

Mujahid said: this occurred in the region of Kufah. Al-Suddi narrated from al-Sha'bi that he used to swear by Allah that the oven appeared only from the region of Kufah. He said: Noah built the ship in the middle of the mosque of Kufah, and the oven was on the right of one entering from the direction of the Kindah Gate, and the gushing of the water from it was a sign for Noah and an indication of the destruction of his people.

Muqatil said: that oven was the oven of Adam, and it was in Syria, in a place called 'Ayn Wardah. Ibn Abbas said: "the oven boiled over" in India. The "fawr" is boiling.

﴿We said: "Load into it﴾, that is, into the ship, ﴿two of each pair﴾. The commentators said: by the pairs he meant two, a male and a female. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: every two that cannot do without one another; the Arabs call each of them a "zawj" (pair). It is said: "a pair of sandals" if he has two sandals; similarly, "a pair of doves," and "a pair of shackles." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female.﴾ Some said: by the pairs he meant the types and kinds, and every type is called a zawj. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that he wears / Abu Qudamah is loved for that, both together"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/55.]]

He meant every type and color. Labid said:

"And one [.....] [[Unreadable word.]] the charge of the warriors, a power / and their kinds [........] [[Unreadable word.]] drinks"

meaning colors and kinds. Hafs read here and in Surah al-Mu'minun "min kullin" with tanwin, meaning "from every kind," and took "ithnayn" (two) as emphasis.

﴿And your family﴾, that is, carry your family, your property and your dependents, ﴿except those against whom the word has already been decreed﴾ of destruction, meaning his wife, who was left behind, and his son Canaan.

﴿And those who have believed﴾, meaning carry those who have believed in you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ They differed about their number. Qatadah, al-Hakam, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: there was in the ship only Noah and his wife, and his three sons: Sam, Ham and Japheth, the brothers of Canaan, and their wives, so all of them were eight. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah invoked Allah to change his sperm, and so he produced the black people.

Al-A'mash said: they were seven: Noah, three wives, and his three sons. Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten apart from their wives: Noah, his sons Ham, Sam and Japheth, and six people from among those who had believed with him, and their wives, all together.

Muqatil said: [they were] seventy-two men and women, and his three sons and their wives, so the total was seventy-eight souls, half of them men and half of them women.

Ibn Abbas said: there were eighty people in the ship of Noah, one of them being Jurhum [[Likewise in Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/57. In Tarikh Dimashq (62/267): with them were their families.]].

Muqatil said: Noah carried with him the body of Adam and placed it crosswise between the men and the women. Noah carried all the animals, the sheep, the wild beasts and the birds, and separated them from one another.

Ibn Abbas said: the first animal Noah loaded into the ship was the goose, and the last he loaded was the donkey. When the donkey entered and its chest went in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its legs could not move forward. Noah kept saying to it: "Enter," and it would stand up but not walk, until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter even if the devil is with you." Noah said to him: "What brought you to me, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Did you not say 'Enter even if the devil is with you'?" Noah said: "Get out of my sight, O enemy of Allah." He said: "You have no choice but to carry me with you." So, as they claim, he was on the back of the ship [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/49.]].

In the Tafsir of Malik ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi, who informed me with the chain of narration to Abu al-Qasim and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad (part of it by reading, and he permitted me the rest on more than one occasion), he said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Harawi narrates to us, saying: Jabir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us from him that the snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: "Carry us." Noah said: "You two are the cause of harm, afflictions and pains, so I will not carry you." They said: "Carry us, and we guarantee you that we will not harm anyone who mentions you." So whoever recites, when fearing their harm: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds. Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good. Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾, neither of them will harm him.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 11, verses 23–40**

Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord. ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord.﴾ Qatadah and Ibn Abbas (through Ata) said: they turned in repentance (anabu) and entreated Him. Mujahid said: they found tranquility in His remembrance. Muqatil said: they were sincere. Al-Akhfash [[In Zad al-Masir it is attributed to al-Farra' (4/76). In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (9/21) there is disagreement regarding some of the opinions.]] said: they were humble before Him. It was also said [[This is Ibn Qutaybah, as in Zad al-Masir.]] that they were modest toward Him.

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide.﴾ ﴿The likeness of the two groups—the believer and the disbeliever—is like the blind and the deaf versus the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in likeness? Will you not then remember?﴾ Al-Farra' said: He did not say "Are they equal in likeness" (in the plural), because the blind and the deaf are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the disbeliever, while the hearing and the seeing are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the believer.

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed I am to you a clear warner, that you worship none but Allah. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a painful day."﴾ The people of Makkah, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read the first "innī" as "anni" with a fatha on the alif, meaning "that I" (because). The rest read it with a kasra, "innī," saying: because sending (irsal) carries the meaning of saying.

﴿Painful﴾ (alīm) means ﴿painful﴾ (mu'lim). Muqatil said: Noah was sent, and his Lord commanded him to build the ark when he was six hundred years old. His lifespan was one thousand and fifty years, and he remained calling his people for nine hundred and fifty years. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he remained among them one thousand years less fifty years﴾, that is, remaining among them as a caller.

﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "No one of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed (tabta'is: be grieved) by what they have been doing."﴾ ﴿Indeed I will destroy them and deliver you from them.﴾ Then he invoked against them and said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant (dayyāran).﴾

Hardship against him from them intensified, and miserliness followed miserliness. No generation came except that it was more wicked than the one before it, until the last of them would say: "This is what our fathers and grandfathers had, just like this," as a madman, and they would not accept anything from him. Then he complained of their condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people by night and by day﴾, until he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.﴾ Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged, for they are to be drowned.﴾ That is, after today.

Noah then devoted himself to [building] the ship and withdrew from his people to a mountain, where he cut wood and struck the iron with his hands, and prepared the materials for the ship from pitch and other things that only he could prepare. His people kept passing by him while he was at his work, mocking him and saying: "O Noah, have you become a carpenter after prophethood?" Allah made the wombs of the women barren, so they remained for years without any child being born to them.

He said: The People of the Torah claim that Allah commanded him to build the ship from teak wood, and to make it with a slope, and to coat it with pitch on its bottom and outside, and that its length should be eighty cubits and its width fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, and the cubit is measured to the shoulder. He made it three stories: lower, middle, and upper. He made windows in it, and Noah did as Allah the Exalted commanded him [[The same source: 48.]].

﴿Until when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾, that is, Our punishment came and the water gushed out from the face of the earth. The Arabs call the face of the earth "the oven of the earth." This is because when it was said: "When you see water flowing over the face of the earth, then board, you and whoever follows you." Among those who said this were Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), in explaining ﴿the oven boiled over﴾, said: it means the dawn rose and the light of morning appeared, and from this is the expression "the dawn lit up" (nawwara al-fajr tanwīran). Qatadah said: it is a place on the earth and the highest place in it. Al-Hasan said: by the oven he meant the one in which bread is baked. It was an oven of stone that belonged to Eve, until it came to Noah, and it was said to him: "When you see the water boiling out of the oven, board, you and your companions." Water gushed from the oven, and his wife learned of it and informed him. This is the saying of Mihran [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/33, the saying of al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ata' from Ibn Abbas.]]. It was transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

Mujahid said: this occurred in the region of Kufah. Al-Suddi narrated from al-Sha'bi that he used to swear by Allah that the oven appeared only from the region of Kufah. He said: Noah built the ship in the middle of the mosque of Kufah, and the oven was on the right of one entering from the direction of the Kindah Gate, and the gushing of the water from it was a sign for Noah and an indication of the destruction of his people.

Muqatil said: that oven was the oven of Adam, and it was in Syria, in a place called 'Ayn Wardah. Ibn Abbas said: "the oven boiled over" in India. The "fawr" is boiling.

﴿We said: "Load into it﴾, that is, into the ship, ﴿two of each pair﴾. The commentators said: by the pairs he meant two, a male and a female. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: every two that cannot do without one another; the Arabs call each of them a "zawj" (pair). It is said: "a pair of sandals" if he has two sandals; similarly, "a pair of doves," and "a pair of shackles." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female.﴾ Some said: by the pairs he meant the types and kinds, and every type is called a zawj. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that he wears / Abu Qudamah is loved for that, both together"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/55.]]

He meant every type and color. Labid said:

"And one [.....] [[Unreadable word.]] the charge of the warriors, a power / and their kinds [........] [[Unreadable word.]] drinks"

meaning colors and kinds. Hafs read here and in Surah al-Mu'minun "min kullin" with tanwin, meaning "from every kind," and took "ithnayn" (two) as emphasis.

﴿And your family﴾, that is, carry your family, your property and your dependents, ﴿except those against whom the word has already been decreed﴾ of destruction, meaning his wife, who was left behind, and his son Canaan.

﴿And those who have believed﴾, meaning carry those who have believed in you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ They differed about their number. Qatadah, al-Hakam, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: there was in the ship only Noah and his wife, and his three sons: Sam, Ham and Japheth, the brothers of Canaan, and their wives, so all of them were eight. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah invoked Allah to change his sperm, and so he produced the black people.

Al-A'mash said: they were seven: Noah, three wives, and his three sons. Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten apart from their wives: Noah, his sons Ham, Sam and Japheth, and six people from among those who had believed with him, and their wives, all together.

Muqatil said: [they were] seventy-two men and women, and his three sons and their wives, so the total was seventy-eight souls, half of them men and half of them women.

Ibn Abbas said: there were eighty people in the ship of Noah, one of them being Jurhum [[Likewise in Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/57. In Tarikh Dimashq (62/267): with them were their families.]].

Muqatil said: Noah carried with him the body of Adam and placed it crosswise between the men and the women. Noah carried all the animals, the sheep, the wild beasts and the birds, and separated them from one another.

Ibn Abbas said: the first animal Noah loaded into the ship was the goose, and the last he loaded was the donkey. When the donkey entered and its chest went in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its legs could not move forward. Noah kept saying to it: "Enter," and it would stand up but not walk, until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter even if the devil is with you." Noah said to him: "What brought you to me, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Did you not say 'Enter even if the devil is with you'?" Noah said: "Get out of my sight, O enemy of Allah." He said: "You have no choice but to carry me with you." So, as they claim, he was on the back of the ship [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/49.]].

In the Tafsir of Malik ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi, who informed me with the chain of narration to Abu al-Qasim and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad (part of it by reading, and he permitted me the rest on more than one occasion), he said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Harawi narrates to us, saying: Jabir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us from him that the snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: "Carry us." Noah said: "You two are the cause of harm, afflictions and pains, so I will not carry you." They said: "Carry us, and we guarantee you that we will not harm anyone who mentions you." So whoever recites, when fearing their harm: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds. Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good. Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾, neither of them will harm him.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 11, verses 23–40**

Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord. ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord.﴾ Qatadah and Ibn Abbas (through Ata) said: they turned in repentance (anabu) and entreated Him. Mujahid said: they found tranquility in His remembrance. Muqatil said: they were sincere. Al-Akhfash [[In Zad al-Masir it is attributed to al-Farra' (4/76). In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (9/21) there is disagreement regarding some of the opinions.]] said: they were humble before Him. It was also said [[This is Ibn Qutaybah, as in Zad al-Masir.]] that they were modest toward Him.

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide.﴾ ﴿The likeness of the two groups—the believer and the disbeliever—is like the blind and the deaf versus the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in likeness? Will you not then remember?﴾ Al-Farra' said: He did not say "Are they equal in likeness" (in the plural), because the blind and the deaf are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the disbeliever, while the hearing and the seeing are in the report as if they were one, since they are descriptions of the believer.

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed I am to you a clear warner, that you worship none but Allah. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a painful day."﴾ The people of Makkah, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read the first "innī" as "anni" with a fatha on the alif, meaning "that I" (because). The rest read it with a kasra, "innī," saying: because sending (irsal) carries the meaning of saying.

﴿Painful﴾ (alīm) means ﴿painful﴾ (mu'lim). Muqatil said: Noah was sent, and his Lord commanded him to build the ark when he was six hundred years old. His lifespan was one thousand and fifty years, and he remained calling his people for nine hundred and fifty years. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he remained among them one thousand years less fifty years﴾, that is, remaining among them as a caller.

﴿The chiefs of those who disbelieved from among his people said: "We see you as nothing but a human like ourselves, and we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us, immature in judgment."﴾ That is: human like ourselves (ādamiyyan mithlanā); ﴿the lowest of us﴾ means the basest of us; ﴿immature in judgment﴾ (bādiya al-ra'y) was read by Mujahid, Abu al-Mu'in, Hamzah, Abu 'Amr and Basir with the meaning of bādiya al-ra'y, without deliberation or reflection; that is, they believed without deliberation.

﴿And we see for you no superiority over us; rather we think you are liars.﴾ Noah said: ﴿O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy (guidance and forgiveness) from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you? Shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾ It was made obscure: it became confused and unclear. The people of Kufah read "fa-'ummiyat" with a damma on the ayn and shaddah on the mim, meaning it became unclear and was confused. The meaning of the statement is: the eyes were blinded to the truth. This is like saying: "The ring entered my finger" or "the khuff (boot) entered my foot," while in reality the finger enters the ring and the foot enters the boot. ﴿Shall we compel you to it﴾ means the evidence and mercy. ﴿While you are averse to it﴾ means you do not want it, that is, it is not accepted.

﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth in return for it﴾, that is, for the revelation and conveying the message, which is an allusion to something unmentioned. ﴿My reward is only from Allah.﴾ ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed; indeed they will meet their Lord﴾ with the Resurrection, so He will reward them for their deeds. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾ ﴿And O my people, who will support me against Allah if I drive them away? Then will you not remember?﴾ The "bā'" in ﴿and I will not drive away﴾ is extra (ṣilah).

﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon (tazdarī: despise and belittle) that Allah will never give them any good.﴾ That is: it will be taken away from them. ﴿Allah knows best what is within themselves﴾ of intention, resolve, good and evil. ﴿Indeed I, then, would be among the wrongdoers﴾ if I did that.

﴿They said: "O Noah, you have argued with us and have disputed with us at length, so bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful."﴾ ﴿He said: "Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not escape. My advice will not benefit you, even if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you (yughwiya: destroy and lead astray) — He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned."﴾ ﴿He is your Lord﴾, and the command and judgment belong to Him. This is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah [a rationalist theological school] and the Murji'ah [a theological school on faith and deeds].

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Ibn Abbas said: it refers to Noah. Muqatil said: it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime (my sin and the burden of my affair); you will not be held accountable for my sin, and I am free of what you commit."﴾ ﴿I will not be taken to account for your sins.﴾

﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "No one of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed (tabta'is: be grieved) by what they have been doing."﴾ ﴿Indeed I will destroy them and deliver you from them.﴾ Then he invoked against them and said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant (dayyāran).﴾

﴿And construct the ship﴾ and make the boat ﴿before Our eyes﴾, that is, in Our sight. Al-Dahhak said: in Our view. Muqatil said: with Our knowledge. Al-Rabi' said: in Our hearing [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: in Our protection.]].

﴿And by Our revelation﴾ [according to what We revealed to you]. Ibn Abbas said: this is because he did not know how to construct the ship, so Allah revealed to him that he should build it in the shape of the breast of a bird. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed they are to be drowned﴾ by the flood. He was commanded not to intercede for them with Him, and it was said that this referred to his wife and son.

﴿And he was constructing the ship.﴾ It was said: its meaning is "and he was constructing," and it was said: its meaning is "and he constructed." ﴿Whenever a company of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him.﴾ That is, they mocked him.

He said: ﴿If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule us now, and you will come to know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment (muqīm: enduring).﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Noah (peace be upon him) built the ship over two years. Its length was three hundred cubits, its width was fifty, and its height was thirty cubits. It was made of teak wood. He made it three levels: in the lowest level he placed the wild animals, predators and vermin; in the middle level, the beasts and livestock; and he himself boarded in the top level [.....] [[Unreadable text.]]

, of what was needed from provisions.

It is narrated from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Noah remained among his people one thousand years less fifty years, calling them to Allah. When his time was nearly over, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him, and he planted a tree [it grew greatly and spread in every direction, then he cut it] [[Addition from al-Tabari.]] and cut off what dried out from it. Then he began to build a ship, and his people would pass by him and ask him, and he would say: 'I am building a ship.' They would mock him and say: 'He is building a ship on dry land, how will it sail?' He would say: 'You will come to know.' When he finished it, and the oven boiled over and the water increased in the streets, the mother of a child became anxious for him, for she loved him very dearly. She took him to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she reached two-thirds of it. When the water reached her, she went up until she climbed to the top of the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him with her hands until the water carried them both away. So if Allah had shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."

It was narrated by Ali ibn Zayd ibn Suhan from Yusuf ibn Mihran from Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said to Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both: "If only you would send us a man who witnessed the ship, so he could tell us about it." So he took them until he reached a mound of earth. He took a handful of that earth in his palm and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the shroud of Ham son of Noah." He struck the mound with his staff and said: "Rise by the permission of Allah." Immediately he was standing, shaking the dust from his head, and he had grown gray. Jesus said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No, I died while I was young, but I thought it was the Hour, so that is why I turned gray." He said: "Tell us about the ship of Noah." He said: "Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits, and it had three levels: one level contained the beasts and wild animals, one level contained the humans, and one level contained the birds. When the dung of the animals increased, Allah the Exalted revealed to Noah: 'Rub the tail of the elephant.' He rubbed it, and a male and female pig fell from it, and they came to the dung. When the mouse fell into the ship's bilge and its ropes, it gnawed them, because the mouse had given birth in the ship. Allah the Exalted revealed to Noah: 'Strike between the eyes of the lion.' He struck it, and a cat and a tomcat came out of its nostril, and they went after the mice."

Jesus said to him: "How did Noah know that the lands had drowned?" He said: "He sent the raven to bring him news. It found a carcass and settled on it, so he invoked fear upon it. That is why it does not get used to houses. Then he sent the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and mud on its foot, so he knew that the lands had drowned." He said: "He placed a red collar around its neck and prayed for it that it would be in a palace in safety [[In Tafsir al-Tabari: 'Anas' and 'Aman'.]]." That is why it gets used to houses.

He said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take him to our families so that he may sit with us and speak to us?" He said: "How can one who has no provision follow you?" Then he said to him: "Return by the permission of Allah." He said: So he returned to dust [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/47.]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Ubayd ibn Umayr that he used to tell stories, and they (the people of Noah) would seize him and choke him until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he would say: "My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know." Until they persisted in disobedience, great sin spread upon the earth from them, and they became arrogant toward him, and the affair became arrogant toward him and against them. Hardship against him from them intensified, and miserliness followed miserliness. No generation came except that it was more wicked than the one before it, until the last of them would say: "This is what our fathers and grandfathers had, just like this," as a madman, and they would not accept anything from him. Then he complained of their condition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people by night and by day﴾, until he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.﴾ Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged, for they are to be drowned.﴾ That is, after today.

Noah then devoted himself to [building] the ship and withdrew from his people to a mountain, where he cut wood and struck the iron with his hands, and prepared the materials for the ship from pitch and other things that only he could prepare. His people kept passing by him while he was at his work, mocking him and saying: "O Noah, have you become a carpenter after prophethood?" He said: The People of the Torah claim that Allah commanded him to build the ship from teak wood, and to make it with a slope, and to coat it with pitch on its bottom and outside, and that its length should be eighty cubits and its width fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, and the cubit is measured to the shoulder. He made it three stories: lower, middle, and upper. He made windows in it, and Noah did as Allah the Exalted commanded him [[The same source: 48.]].

﴿Until when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾, that is, Our punishment came and the water gushed out from the face of the earth. The Arabs call the face of the earth "the oven of the earth." This is because when it was said: "When you see water flowing over the face of the earth, then board, you and whoever follows you." It was transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

Mujahid said: this occurred in the region of Kufah. Al-Suddi narrated from al-Sha'bi that he used to swear by Allah that the oven appeared only from the region of Kufah. He said: Noah built the ship in the middle of the mosque of Kufah, and the oven was on the right of one entering from the direction of the Kindah Gate, and the gushing of the water from it was a sign for Noah and an indication of the destruction of his people.

Muqatil said: that oven was the oven of Adam, and it was in Syria, in a place called 'Ayn Wardah. Ibn Abbas said: "the oven boiled over" in India. The "fawr" is boiling.

﴿We said: "Load into it﴾, that is, into the ship, ﴿two of each pair﴾. The commentators said: by the pairs he meant two, a male and a female. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: every two that cannot do without one another; the Arabs call each of them a "zawj" (pair). It is said: "a pair of sandals" if he has two sandals; similarly, "a pair of doves," and "a pair of shackles." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female.﴾ Some said: by the pairs he meant the types and kinds, and every type is called a zawj. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that he wears / Abu Qudamah is loved for that, both together"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/55.]]

He meant every type and color. Labid said:

"And one [.....] [[Unreadable word.]] the charge of the warriors, a power / and their kinds [........] [[Unreadable word.]] drinks"

meaning colors and kinds. Hafs read here and in Surah al-Mu'minun "min kullin" with tanwin, meaning "from every kind," and took "ithnayn" (two) as emphasis.

﴿And your family﴾, that is, carry your family, your property and your dependents, ﴿except those against whom the word has already been decreed﴾ of destruction, meaning his wife, who was left behind, and his son Canaan.

﴿And those who have believed﴾, meaning carry those who have believed in you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾ They differed about their number. Qatadah, al-Hakam, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: there was in the ship only Noah and his wife, and his three sons: Sam, Ham and Japheth, the brothers of Canaan, and their wives, so all of them were eight. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah invoked Allah to change his sperm, and so he produced the black people.

Al-A'mash said: they were seven: Noah, three wives, and his three sons. Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten apart from their wives: Noah, his sons Ham, Sam and Japheth, and six people from among those who had believed with him, and their wives, all together.

Muqatil said: Noah carried with him the body of Adam and placed it crosswise between the men and the women. Noah carried all the animals, the sheep, the wild beasts and the birds, and separated them from one another.

When the donkey entered and its chest went in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its legs could not move forward. Noah kept saying to it: "Enter," and it would stand up but not walk, until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter even if the devil is with you." Noah said to him: "What brought you to me, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Did you not say 'Enter even if the devil is with you'?" Noah said: "Get out of my sight, O enemy of Allah." He said: "You have no choice but to carry me with you." So, as they claim, he was on the back of the ship [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/49.]].

In the Tafsir of Malik ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi, who informed me with the chain of narration to Abu al-Qasim and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad (part of it by reading, and he permitted me the rest on more than one occasion), he said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Harawi narrates to us, saying: Jabir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us from him that the snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: "Carry us." Noah said: "You two are the cause of harm, afflictions and pains, so I will not carry you." They said: "Carry us, and we guarantee you that we will not harm anyone who mentions you." So whoever recites, when fearing their harm: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds. Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good. Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾, neither of them will harm him.

And Noah said, "Board it; in the name of God is its course and its mooring." Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read: "mujrahā wa-mursāhā" with both mīms vowelled with a ḍamma and the rāʾ and sīn vowelled with a kasra, and this is the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "majrāhā" means where it runs, and "mursāhā" means where it comes to rest, that is, where it stops in the water.

Muhammad ibn Muhaysin read both mīms with a fatḥa, and both are verbal nouns (maṣdar). The meaning is that God, exalted is He, holds in His hand its running and its mooring, that is its stability. One says jarā yajrī jarīyan wa-majrā, and rasā yarsū rusūwan wa-mursā, like dhahaba madhhaban and ḍaraba maḍrabā. Imru' al-Qays said:

"I passed beyond guards and the terrors of a people,
who would be forbidden to me if they kept my death secret."

That is, my killing (qatlī).

The rest read both mīms with a ḍamma, and this was chosen by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim. Its meaning is: "In the name of God is its running and its mooring," like God's words, "Cause me to land a blessed landing, and cause me to enter a sincere entrance and bring me out a sincere exit" (23:29 / 17:80), in the sense of the act of landing, entering and exiting.

"Indeed my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful." Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: When Noah wanted it to moor, he said, "In the name of God," and it moored; and when he wanted it to run, he said, "In the name of God," and it ran.

﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains.﴾ And Noah called out to his son, Kanʿan, and he was defiant (ʿanīdan). It was said: he was also an unbeliever.

﴿And he was apart from him,﴾ he did not board the ship with him.

my heart has become enamoured of him."

That is, enamoured (maftūnan).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 11, verses 49–60:

﴿Those are some of the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this.﴾ That is, the things I have told you about, O Muhammad, were unknown to you and to your people before my informing you of them. ﴿So be patient.﴾ Persevere in carrying out God's command and conveying His message, and in bearing the harm the disbelievers inflict, as Noah was patient. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome is for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin).﴾ That is, the final result, at the end of the affair, is happiness, victory and forgiveness, as it was for the believers among Noah's people and the other nations.

﴿And to ʿAd [We sent] their brother Hud.﴾ That is, We sent to ʿAd their brother Hud, a brother by lineage, not by religion. ﴿He said: "O my people, worship God.﴾ Affirm God's oneness and increase your worship; in the Qur'an "worship" carries the sense of monotheism. ﴿You have no god other than Him. You are but fabricators.﴾ You, in associating idols with Him, are only liars.

﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾ for conveying the message, ﴿nor do I seek any reward. My reward is only from the One who created me (fatarani).﴾ Fitra means the initial creation. ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ This is because the peoples used to say to the messengers: "You want nothing but to take our wealth," and the messengers replied to them with this.

﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ that is, believe in Him and He will forgive you; here seeking forgiveness means faith. ﴿Then turn to Him in repentance﴾ from your worship of other than Him and from your past sins. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "and repent to Him," because repentance is seeking forgiveness and seeking forgiveness is repentance. ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾ meaning in succession. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Khuzaymah ibn Kaysan said: copious and plentiful. ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾ power added to your power, might with your might. This is because God withheld rain from them for years and made the wombs of their women barren for three years, so Hud said to them: "If you believe, God will bring your lands back to life and give you wealth and children."

﴿And do not turn away﴾ do not retreat as those who associate partners with God. ﴿They said: "O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof (bayyina)," clarity and demonstration for what you say, so that we would acknowledge it and submit to you. ﴿And we will not abandon our gods because of your words﴾ that is, because of your saying. The Arabs place the preposition bi (ب) in the place of ʿan (عن), and ʿan in the place of bi.

﴿And we will not believe you﴾ we will not accept you as truthful. ﴿We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil﴾ meaning: you do not engage in what you engage in, opposing us and reviling our gods, except that some of our gods have struck you and afflicted you with harm, rather madness and delirium, which drive you to what you say and do. We say nothing about you except this and we attribute your affair to nothing but this. Hud said to them: ﴿I call God to witness, and bear witness yourselves that I am free of what you associate with Him﴾ meaning the idols. ﴿So scheme against me all together, and give me no respite.﴾ Plot against me, you and your idols together, to harm and deceive me. ﴿I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock.﴾

Al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and causes it to die. Al-Farra' said: He owns it and has power over it. Al-Qutabi said: He subdues it, because whoever has his forelock seized has been overpowered. Ibn Jarir said: He singled out the forelock because the Arabs use this expression when describing a person as humbled and submissive; they say, "the forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning he obeys him and he directs him as he wishes. When they took a captive and then wished to release him and bestow favour upon him, they would cut his forelock so that they could boast of this over him. So He addressed them in terms they understood from their own speech.

﴿Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.﴾ He says: indeed my Lord is upon the path of truth; He rewards the doer of good with his goodness and the doer of evil with his disobedience, and He does not wrong anyone at all, and He accepts nothing but Islam. The phrase implies a supplied "that I": "indeed my Lord guides, or urges, or leads you onto a straight path."

﴿But if you turn away, I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with.﴾ That is, say, O Muhammad: I have conveyed to you what I was sent to you with. ﴿And my Lord will replace you with another people﴾ who affirm His oneness and worship Him. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾ by your turning away and opposition; you harm only yourselves. It was said: its meaning is that you cannot cause Him any good if He wishes to misguide you. Abdullah recited: "and your destruction will not harm Him when He destroys you, nor will you diminish Him at all," because whether you exist or not is the same to Him.

﴿Indeed, my Lord is over all things a Guardian.﴾ That is, for every thing a guardian; here ʿalā (على) is in the sense of lam (ل). He guards me from your reaching me with harm.

﴿And when Our command came﴾ that is, Our punishment, ﴿We saved Hud and those who believed with him﴾ and they were four thousand, ﴿by mercy from Us﴾ by a blessing from Us, ﴿and We saved them from a harsh punishment.﴾ It was said: this was the wind. It was also said: the harsh punishment means the punishment of the Resurrection; that is, just as We saved them from punishment in this world, so We saved them from punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿And those were ʿAd﴾ He refers to them as a tribe. ﴿They denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers﴾ meaning Hud alone, because no messenger other than Hud was sent to them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ meaning the Prophet (ﷺ), since there was no messenger in his time other than him. Here the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers.

﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾ arrogant, who does not accept the truth nor submit to it. Abu ʿUbayd said: al-ʿanid, al-ʿanud, al-ʿashir and al-muʿanid all mean one who opposes you with contrariness; from this the vein that gushes blood and cannot be stopped is called ʿirq ʿanid. The rajaz poet said:

"I am old, I cannot bear the ʿandā [the burden]" [Lisan al-Arab: 3/307; its opening line is: "When you journey, make me the middle one."]

﴿And they were pursued with a curse in this world﴾ meaning distance from mercy, punishment and destruction. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾ that is, and on the Day of Resurrection likewise. Thus they were cursed in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed ʿAd disbelieved their Lord﴾ that is, disbelieved in their Lord, as one says "I thanked him" and "I thanked him for it," "I disbelieved him" and "I disbelieved in him," "I advised him" and "I advised him for it." It was said: the meaning is "they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord."

﴿Unquestionably, away with ʿAd, the people of Hud!﴾ Distance (bu'd) has two meanings: one is distance as opposed to nearness, as one says "he was far (baʿuda, yabʿudu, buʿdan)"; the other means destruction, from which one says "he perished (baʿuda, yabʿudu, buʿdan wa-buʿdan)."

The Angels, the Messengers of Our Lord, came to Abraham (Ibrahim) with good news ... (Qur'an 11:69)

Scholars differed about how many they were. Ibn 'Abbas said there were three: Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael) and Israfil (Seraphiel). al-Dahhak said nine, and al-Suddi said eleven. They appeared in the form of handsome young men with bright faces.

To Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) with the glad tidings: the good news of Isaac and Ya'qub (Jacob), and of the destruction of the people of Lot. They said, "Salaman" (peace). They greeted him with peace. The word salaman is in the accusative because it is the object of the verb of saying, since salam is a form of speech; that is, they said and greeted with "salaman." He (Abraham) said, "Salamun" (peace), meaning "upon you be peace." It was also said that it means "for you is peace." It was also said that it is in the nominative as a reported speech (al-hikayah, direct quotation of what was said). "It was said: Praise be to God" and "Say: Hittatun" (Qur'an 2:58 and 7:161 are alluded to here as the same wording).

Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "silam" with a kasra on the sin and without an alif, and likewise in al-Dhariyat. It is also so in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud. Its meaning: "We are a peace suitable for you, not a war." It was also said that it means peace (al-silm) as well, just as one says hill and halal, and haram and haram. al-Farra' recited:

"We passed by and said, 'Peace upon you,' and so they replied, as the clouds reply to the lightning, the bright ones."

So he (Abraham) did not delay, that is, he did not tarry or remain, and Abraham came with a roasted calf. The particle an here means "until," with the preposition dropped, that is, "until he came with a calf roasted." Ibn 'Abbas said: roasted on hot stones in a pit in the ground. Qatadah and Mujahid said: cooked with stones and roasted. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: part of it was roasted with stones. Abu 'Ubaydah said: whatever you heat, you have hanadhtahu, so it is hanidh and mahnudh. The root of yahnudh is that when you place it on the embers, some of it on top of others, so it sweats (li-ta'riq). [Lisan al-'Arab (3/485): it is to bring it to the fire for a stretch or two and then cover it with cinders in the sun so it sweats beneath them; it is then mahnudh and hanidh. If it does not sweat, it is said to be kaba.]

So when he saw their hands not reaching to it, that is, to the calf, he found them strange (nakiruhum). That is, he disliked them. It is said: nakirtu al-shay' and ankartuhu have the same meaning. al-A'sha said:

"She disowned me, and what she disowned was not among the events except the grey hair and baldness."

So he combined the two meanings at one time.

And he sensed fear of them (awjasa minhum khifah). He concealed and felt fear of them. Muqatil said: it fell into his heart. al-Akhfash said: it lodged in his self. al-Farra' said: he felt it (istash'ara). al-Hasan said: he spoke to himself. The root of awjasa is "entering," and fear had entered his heart. Qatadah said: that was because when a guest came to them and did not eat their food, they thought he had not come for good, and that he was harboring evil.

They said, "Do not fear, O Abraham, for we are the Angels of God. We have been sent to the people of Lot." al-Walibi said: when Abraham knew that they were angels, he feared that he and his people were the intended targets of punishment, because the angels used to descend at that time with punishment, like the verse in al-Hijr: "We do not send down the angels except with truth," that is, with punishment. The angels said, "Do not fear, we have been sent to the people of Lot," not to your people.

And his wife Sarah, daughter of Haran, son of Nahur, son of Sarugh, son of Arghu, son of Faligh, and she was the cousin of Abraham, was standing behind the curtain, listening to the speech of the angels and the speech of Abraham. It was also said: she was standing (......) [Unreadable word.]

the Messengers while Abraham was sitting with them, so this is primary speech (kalam awwali, the speech as originally uttered). Ibn Mas'ud read: "and his wife was standing" while he was sitting, and she laughed (fadahikat).

They differed about the cause that brought about the laughter. al-Suddi said: when the food was brought near them and they did not eat, Abraham feared and suspected they were thieves, so he said to them, "Will you not eat?" They said, "O Abraham, we do not eat food except for a price." He said, "For this there is a price." They said, "And what is its price?" He said, "You mention the name of God at its beginning and praise Him at its end." Then Jibril looked at Mika'il and said, "He deserves to be taken as a friend (khalil)." When Abraham and Sarah saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange ... so Sarah laughed and said, "We stood to serve our guests, these, we serve them ourselves out of honor for them, and they do not eat our food."

Qatadah said: she laughed at the heedlessness of the people of Lot and the nearness of punishment to them. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: she laughed out of Abraham's fear of the three men, while he was among his servants and retinue. Ibn 'Abbas and Wahb said: she laughed in wonder that she should have a child in her old age and the old age of her husband. They said: this is of the inverted order (taqdim alladhi ma'nahu al-ta'khir), and it meant: [.....] [Unreadable word.]

And his wife was standing.

So We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Ya'qub (Jacob). So she laughed and said, "Woe to me! Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman?" (Qur'an 11:71-72). It was also said: she laughed for joy at being secure from them when they said, "Do not fear." Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: "fadahikat" means she menstruated at that time. The Arabs say: "the hare laughed" when it menstruates. A poet said:

"The hares laughed upon the rock, like the blood of fear on the day of meeting."

So We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Ya'qub. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Sha'bi said: al-wara' is the child's child. The reciters differed concerning His words "Ya'qub." Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim put it in the accusative, and it was said it is in the genitive position as an adjective, that is, "from after Isaac with Ya'qub." When the preposition was dropped, it became accusative. It was also said it is governed by an implied verb: "and We granted him Ya'qub." Others read it in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject. So when she was given the good news of the son and the grandson, she struck her face (sakkat wajhaha), that is, she slapped it out of wonder, and said, "Woe to me!" The original is "ya wailata," meaning "O my woe," "shall I bear a child while I am an old woman?" It is said she was ninety years old according to Ibn Ishaq, and ninety-nine years old according to Mujahid.

"And this is my husband (ba'li), my spouse." He was called ba'l because he is the manager of her affairs, just as the owner of a thing is called ba'l. A palm tree that is sustained by rain rather than by river water is called ba'l. "An old man (shaykhan)." Abraham was a hundred years old according to Mujahid, and a hundred and twenty according to Ibn Ishaq.
